nota: F141–F148. CRS, nota 26: 'net annual revenues for the United States would increase by about $180 million to $280 million' (U.S. Entity, Recent Study Results, June 2012, pp. 6-7); a mesma nota dá o valor da parte do Canadá em '$229 million-$335 million annually' (fora da tela). BC Hydro 2026, p. 7: 'typically worth between $110 - $400 million per year', sem moeda: a tela sem '$' (como o espelho pede) ou 'C$/US$' só se a fonte disser. Sugiro tirar '(CANADIAN ENTITY)' de 'DISPUTED BY BRITISH COLUMBIA': a entidade designada é a BC Hydro (CRS, nota 2), e quem contesta é a província.

texto_aprovado: Each side has its own account of what the other gains. The American agencies that run the treaty once estimated that ending it would raise American power revenues, mostly by ending Canada's share. British Columbia disputed those assumptions. Its argument is that the treaty makes the river dependable, and that a dependable river is worth more to the United States than the share it sends north. Two careful sums, and they don't land in the same place.
